fanoutqa_029852.t: Shiba Inu :: In popular culture :: chunk_0006
fanoutqa_029852.x:
Shiba Inu :: In popular culture :: chunk_0006
Despite not being a popular dog breed outside of Japan, the Shiba Inu has become popular on the Internet. [Doge](/wiki/Doge_(meme) "Doge (meme)") is an [Internet meme](/wiki/Internet_meme "Internet meme") from 2013 characterized by [Kabosu](/wiki/Kabosu_(dog) "Kabosu (dog)"), a Shiba Inu, and [broken English](/wiki/Broken_English "Broken English"). A [cryptocurrency](/wiki/Cryptocurrency "Cryptocurrency"), [Dogecoin](/wiki/Dogecoin "Dogecoin"), is named after this meme, and its logo bears an image of Kabosu. Another cryptocurrency is also named [Shiba Inu](/wiki/Shiba_Inu_(cryptocurrency) "Shiba Inu (cryptocurrency)") after the breed. Another Shiba Inu that went viral was a dog known as [Cheems](/wiki/Cheems "Cheems"). He went viral during the [COVID-19 pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") and gained worldwide attention. Cheems died during cancer surgery on August 18, 2023 at the age of 12½ years.[[41]](#cite_note-41) In December 2024, a man by the name of Kantaro Inagaki began to document his walks across Japan with a Shiba Inu named San-chan.[[42]](#cite_note-42)

The breed is often referred to as *Shibe* in memes. According to Jamie Cohen, an assistant professor of media studies at [Queens College](/wiki/Queens_College "Queens College") of the [City University of New York](/wiki/City_University_of_New_York "City University of New York"), the Shiba Inu breed has had a significant presence in online culture since at least 2010.[[43]](#cite_note-grid-43)

fanoutqa_011420.x:
Gansu :: History :: Republican China :: chunk_0008
As a result of frequent earthquakes, droughts and famines, the economic progress of Gansu was significantly slower than that of other provinces of China until recently. Based on the area's abundant mineral resources it has begun developing into a vital industrial center. An [earthquake in Gansu](/wiki/1920_Haiyuan_earthquake "1920 Haiyuan earthquake") at 8.6 on the [Richter scale](/wiki/Richter_magnitude_scale "Richter magnitude scale") killed around 180,000 people mostly in the present-day area of [Ningxia](/wiki/Ningxia "Ningxia") in 1920, and [another with a magnitude of 7.6](/wiki/1932_Changma_earthquake "1932 Changma earthquake") killed 275 in 1932.[[15]](#cite_note-NGDC-16)

The [Muslim Conflict in Gansu (1927–1930)](/wiki/Muslim_Conflict_in_Gansu_(1927%E2%80%931930) "Muslim Conflict in Gansu (1927–1930)") was a conflict against the [Guominjun](/wiki/Guominjun "Guominjun").

While the Muslim General [Ma Hongbin](/wiki/Ma_Hongbin "Ma Hongbin") was acting chairman of the province, Muslim General [Ma Buqing](/wiki/Ma_Buqing "Ma Buqing") was in virtual control of Gansu in 1940. Liangzhou District in [Wuwei](/wiki/Wuwei,_Gansu "Wuwei, Gansu") was previously his headquarters in Gansu, where he controlled 15 million Muslims.[[16]](#cite_note-17) [Xinjiang](/wiki/Xinjiang "Xinjiang") came under [Kuomintang](/wiki/Kuomintang "Kuomintang") (Nationalist) control after their soldiers entered via Gansu.[[17]](#cite_note-Lin2010-18) Gansu's [Tienshui](/wiki/Tianshui "Tianshui") was the site of a Japanese-Chinese warplane fight.[[18]](#cite_note-Armstrong2006-19)

Gansu was vulnerable to Soviet penetration via Xinjiang.[[19]](#cite_note-Fleming2014-20) Gansu was a passageway for [Soviet war supplies for the Republic of China](/wiki/Sino-Soviet_Non-Aggression_Pact "Sino-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact") during the [Second Sino-Japanese War](/wiki/Second_Sino-Japanese_War "Second Sino-Japanese War").[[20]](#cite_note-Forbes1986-21)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/Main_Building_HIT.jpg/250px-Main_Building_HIT.jpg)](/wiki/File:Main_Building_HIT.jpg)

Main of Building HIT

Key honors include the following:[[3]](#cite_note-:4-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4)

* In 1920, the Harbin Institute of Technology was originally established as the Harbin Sino-Russian School for Industry to educate railway engineers.[[5]](#cite_note-5)
* In 1931, postgraduate students were enrolled from the spring of 1931.
* In 1935, during the Japanese invasion of China, the university fell under Japanese control.
* On January 1, 1938, the name Harbin Institute of Technology was reinstated, which it has retained until the present.
* In 1945, after the Japanese defeated in World War II and evacuated, HIT was headed by the Zhongchang Railway Bureau and jointly managed by China and the Soviet Union.
* In 1949, Harbin Institute of technology recruited graduate students from all over the country. It is one of the earliest institutions to train postgraduates in China.
* In 1951, HIT was approved by the central government to become one of the two institutions of higher learning to learn advanced techniques from the USSR. HIT enjoyed a reputation as the 'Cradle for Engineers'.
* In 1954, HIT was established as one of six [national key universities](/wiki/National_Key_Universities "National Key Universities") of China, the only one outside [Beijing](/wiki/Beijing "Beijing").[[3]](#cite_note-:4-3)
* In 1984, HIT became one of 15 national major investment universities of China. In 1984, HIT became one of the first 22 universities to establish a graduate school.
* In 1996, HIT was established as a first-class university under [Project 211](/wiki/Project_211 "Project 211") (a project of [National Key Universities](/wiki/National_Key_Universities "National Key Universities") initiated by the [Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China](/wiki/Ministry_of_Ed

fanoutqa_023452.t: David J. Wineland :: Early life and career :: chunk_0001
fanoutqa_023452.x:
David J. Wineland :: Early life and career :: chunk_0001
Wineland was born in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin. He lived in Denver until he was three years old, at which time his family moved to [Sacramento, California](/wiki/Sacramento,_California "Sacramento, California").[[5]](#cite_note-NIST-PR-5) Wineland graduated from [Encina High School](/wiki/Encina_High_School "Encina High School") in Sacramento in 1961.[[6]](#cite_note-r1-6) In Sept. 1961–Dec. 1963, he studied at [University of California, Davis](/wiki/University_of_California,_Davis "University of California, Davis"). He received his bachelor's degree in physics from the [University of California, Berkeley](/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley") in 1965 and his master's and doctoral degrees in physics from [Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University").[[5]](#cite_note-NIST-PR-5) He completed his PhD in 1970, supervised by [Norman Foster Ramsey, Jr.](/wiki/Norman_Foster_Ramsey,_Jr. "Norman Foster Ramsey, Jr.")[[7]](#cite_note-7) His doctoral dissertation is titled "The Atomic Deuterium Maser". He then performed postdoctoral research in [Hans Dehmelt](/wiki/Hans_Dehmelt "Hans Dehmelt")'s group at the [University of Washington](/wiki/University_of_Washington "University of Washington") where he investigated electrons in [ion traps](/wiki/Ion_trap "Ion trap"). In 1975, he joined the National Bureau of Standards (now called [NIST](/wiki/NIST "NIST")), where he started the ion storage group and is on the physics faculty of the [University of Colorado at Boulder](/wiki/University_of_Colorado_at_Boulder "University of Colorado at Boulder"). In January 2018, Wineland moved to the Department of Physics [University of Oregon](/wiki/University_of_Oregon "University of Oregon") as a [Knight Research Professor](/wiki/Philip_H._Knight_Chairs_and_Professorships "Philip H. Knight Chairs and Professorships"),[[8]](#cite_note-8) while still being engaged with the Ion Storag

fanoutqa_031132.x:
Rain of animals :: History :: chunk_0001
Rain of flightless animals and things has been reported throughout history.[[1]](#cite_note-Library_of_Congress-1) In the [Bible](/wiki/Bible "Bible"), a rain of frogs is described as one of the [ten plagues of Egypt](/wiki/Plagues_of_Egypt "Plagues of Egypt"). The Bible also mentions other similar events, such as [quail](/wiki/Quail "Quail") falling from the sky to save the Hebrews from hunger in Exodus 16:13. In the fourth century BC, the Greek [Athenaeus](/wiki/Athenaeus "Athenaeus") mentioned a rain of fish that lasted three days in the region of [Chaeronea](/wiki/Chaeronea "Chaeronea") in the [Peloponnese](/wiki/Peloponnese "Peloponnese").[[4]](#cite_note-:1-4) In the [Middle Ages](/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages"), the frequency of the phenomenon in certain regions led locals to imagine that fish were born in the skies before falling into the sea.[[4]](#cite_note-:1-4)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Wea02218_-_Flickr_-_NOAA_Photo_Library.jpg/250px-Wea02218_-_Flickr_-_NOAA_Photo_Library.jpg)](/wiki/File:Wea02218_-_Flickr_-_NOAA_Photo_Library.jpg)

Raining snakes, 1680

In 1625, a rain of frogs was reported to have hit [Tournai](/wiki/Tournai "Tournai"), [Belgium](/wiki/Belgium "Belgium").[[5]](#cite_note-5) In 1794, French soldiers saw toads fall from the sky during heavy rain at Lalain, near the French city of [Lille](/wiki/Lille "Lille").[[6]](#cite_note-Popular_Mechanics-6) Rural inhabitants in [Yoro](/wiki/Yoro "Yoro"), Honduras claim "fish rain" happens there every summer, a phenomenon they call the [lluvia de peces](/wiki/Lluvia_de_peces "Lluvia de peces"), although the name may be indoctrination from a Spanish missionary as the fish have only been found near tributaries after storms.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

fanoutqa_039324.t: David Card :: Contributions to Economics of Education :: chunk_0003
fanoutqa_039324.x:
David Card :: Contributions to Economics of Education :: chunk_0003
David Card has made influential contributions to the economics of education by studying how access and school environments affect long-term outcomes. In one of his studies, Card used proximity to colleges as an instrumental variable. Results showed that people who lived closer to universities were more likely to enroll. Because of the additional years of schooling, this translated into higher earnings.[[19]](#cite_note-:2-19) Card’s work helped prove that there are other factors that affect earnings and play a key role, like schooling. He also found that smaller class sizes, staff income, and resources can affect students' prospects, especially for those from disadvantaged backgrounds.[[23]](#cite_note-23) His findings encouraged economists to consider how educational environments can affect inequality over time, and his studies helped broaden how economists think about education by highlighting the importance of real-world variation, institutional differences, and student experiences. His work played an important role in shifting the field toward a more careful empirical design and helped establish education as an area where credible causal evidence could be used to understand economic mobility and opportunity. These contributions were part of a broader empirical movement recognized when Card received the 2021 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics Sciences.[[6]](#cite_note-:0-6)[[8]](#cite_note-:1-8)
